title: Target-etale locality of qcqs and universal homeomorphism for algebraic stacks
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], and let $f:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. Let $(u_i:W_i\to\mathcal B)_{i\in I}$ be a small jointly surjective family of representable etale morphisms from algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Representable means that every scheme base change is an algebraic space; etale is tested on etale scheme charts. Joint surjectivity means that every field-valued target object lifts to some $W_i$ after a field extension. Form $f_i:\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}W_i\to W_i$, with 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Use quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of [def-sfb-stack-qcqs-morphism]; in particular quasi-separatedness requires the relative diagonal to be quasi-compact and quasi-separated as a representable morphism. Give point spaces the atlas topology of [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology]. A universal homeomorphism means a morphism whose every base change by an algebraic stack induces a homeomorphism of point spaces. For each of the three properties quasi-compact, quasi-separated, and universal homeomorphism, separately, $f$ has that property if and only if every $f_i$ has it. Each of these properties is preserved by arbitrary base change by an algebraic stack. No Deligne--Mumford, finite-inertia, finite-type or representability hypothesis on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tags 06TZ (lemma-check-separated-covering, including quasi-separatedness), 0DTL (lemma-check-quasi-compact-covering), 0DTQ (lemma-check-universal-homeomorphism-covering); base-change Tags 050F (lemma-base-change-separated), 050V (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact), 0CI8 (lemma-base-change-universal-homeomorphism). Family version by algebraic-space coproduct and open-locality on its disjoint components.

proof.text: All fibre products below are algebraic stacks by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products]. Base change preserves quasi-compactness directly: for $\mathcal B\prime\to\mathcal B$ and a quasi-compact test $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal B\prime$, $(\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal B\prime)\times_{\mathcal B\prime}\mathcal Z\simeq\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal Z$. The same associativity proves preservation of universal homeomorphisms, since after any further base change the point map is a point map already required to be a homeomorphism for $f$. These identifications are obtained by composing the isomorphisms in the defining triples of the 2-fibre product; reversing them inserts the given projection to $\mathcal B\prime$. Thus these two properties imply the corresponding properties for all $f_i$.

Assume every $f_i$ is quasi-compact. Fix a quasi-compact test $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal B$. Choose an affine smooth surjective atlas $C\to\mathcal Z$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection]. For each $i$, $C\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$ is an algebraic space, since $u_i$ is representable. Choose a disjoint-affine etale atlas $\coprod_a V_{ia}\to C\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$ by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]. The maps $V_{ia}\to C$ are etale, hence flat and locally finitely presented; their point images are open by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open]. Their images jointly cover $|C|$: lift a field-valued image in $\mathcal B$ to some $W_i$ after extension, include the isomorphism to form the fibre-product object, and lift again to the atlas. Since $C$ is affine it is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs], so finitely many $V_j=V_{i_j a_j}$ suffice. No $W_i$, or its atlas, has been assumed quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 0DTL (lemma-check-quasi-compact-covering), finite affine refinement of its U; family version

proof.text: Each $V_j$ is a quasi-compact scheme, hence a quasi-compact stack (its identity is a smooth atlas). The map $V_j\to W_{i_j}$ and quasi-compactness of $f_{i_j}$ give quasi-compact $\mathcal H_j=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}V_j$. Choose an affine smooth surjective scheme atlas $H_j\to\mathcal H_j$. The finite coproduct $H=\coprod_j H_j$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-affine-coproduct-spectrum], and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. It maps surjectively to $\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal Z$: lift its $\mathcal Z$-component to $C$, then to one of the covering $V_j$, retaining all isomorphisms, and finally to $H_j$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-quasicompact-surjection] the target is quasi-compact. As $\mathcal Z$ was arbitrary this proves quasi-compactness of $f$. The empty finite coproduct handles the empty test stack.

source.place: Tag 0DTL, last two sentences; Tag 04YC (lemma-quasi-compact-stack), surjective image criterion

proof.text: We will use the following two-line consequence for algebraic spaces. For $h:E\to T$, quasi-separated means quasi-compactness of $d:E\to E\times_T E$. If $T\prime\to T$ is any space map, $d\prime$ is the pullback of $d$ along $(E\times_T E)\times_T T\prime\to E\times_T E$: on sections both sides consist of a pair of equal sections of $E$ with their chosen section of $T\prime$. Apply base-change stability of quasi-compactness in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-fppf-local]. For a jointly surjective flat locally finitely presented family $T_i\to T$, the analogous maps $(E\times_T E)\times_T T_i\to E\times_T E$ form such a family; apply descent of quasi-compactness in that same node to $d$. Thus quasi-separatedness of space maps is stable under base change and is checked on such families. The quasi-compact assertion itself is precisely the cited node.

source.place: Tags 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated) and 041N (lemma-descending-property-quasi-separated), expanding the diagonal reduction

proof.text: Put $D=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal A$. The relative-inertia geometry node makes $\Delta_f$ representable, and the groupoid diagonal identities node identifies $\Delta_{f_i}$ with its base change to $D_i=D\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$. If $f$ is quasi-separated, every space-valued scheme test of $\Delta_f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated; step 4 preserves both properties under space base change, and hence under arbitrary stack base change after taking scheme tests. This proves stability of quasi-separatedness, and the forward locality implication. Conversely assume every $f_i$ is quasi-separated. For any scheme $T\to D$, write $E=\mathcal A\times_D T$, a space. The $T_i=T\times_D D_i=T\times_{\mathcal B}W_i$ are spaces and form a jointly surjective etale family over $T$. Their pullbacks $E\times_T T_i\to T_i$ have both properties, by the diagonal square and step 4 applied to scheme charts of $T_i$ (the cited space quasi-compactness descent checks these charts). Step 4 then descends both properties to $E\to T$. This holds for every $T$, exactly the definition of quasi-separatedness of $f$.

source.place: Tags 06TZ (lemma-check-separated-covering), 050F (lemma-base-change-separated); scheme-test expansion for the family

proof.text: Assume every $f_i$ is a universal homeomorphism and fix any $\mathcal Z\to\mathcal B$. Put $P=\mathcal A\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal Z$. Choose smooth surjective scheme atlases $U_i\to W_i\times_{\mathcal B}\mathcal Z$. The maps $q_i:U_i\to\mathcal Z$ are representable smooth, and jointly surjective. Let $P_i=P\times_{\mathcal Z}U_i$. The maps $h_i:|P_i|\to|U_i|$ are homeomorphisms, because the stack maps are base changes of $f_i$ (associate the defining triples). The maps $p_i:P_i\to P$ are representable smooth and jointly surjective, by base-change and composition permanence. The field-extension lifting definition proves joint surjectivity also on point classes.

source.place: Tag 0DTQ (lemma-check-universal-homeomorphism-covering), choice of U and diagram; family version

proof.text: The point maps $|q_i|$ and $|p_i|$ are open. For $q_i$ this is [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology-flat-lfp-open], since its source is a scheme and it is smooth, hence flat and locally finitely presented. For $p_i$ choose a smooth surjective scheme atlas $V\to P_i$. Its composite $V\to P$ has the same properties, so is open by that node. For an open $O\subseteq|P_i|$, its inverse image in $|V|$ is open by continuity, and its image under $|V|\to|P|$ is exactly $|p_i|(O)$ by atlas surjectivity. Hence $|p_i|(O)$ is open. All point maps, in particular $h:|P|\to|\mathcal Z|$, are continuous by [lem-sfb-stack-point-topology].

source.place: Tag 0DTQ, openness of the horizontal arrows, expanded by smooth scheme atlases

proof.text: The map $h$ is surjective: lift a target point to a $U_i$ and use the surjectivity of $h_i$. It is injective: if two points of $P$ have the same image, their field-valued representatives have isomorphic images after a common extension. Lift that common target object to a $U_i$ after another extension. Both representatives, with these isomorphisms, are then points of $P_i$ over the same point of $U_i$. Injectivity of $h_i$ identifies their classes in $P_i$, so their projected classes in $P$ agree. For an open $O\subseteq|P|$ one has $h(O)=\bigcup_i |q_i|\bigl(h_i(|p_i|^{-1}(O))\bigr)$, by joint surjectivity of the $p_i$. Each term is open by continuity of $p_i$, the homeomorphism $h_i$, and openness of $q_i$. Thus $h$ is an open continuous bijection and is a homeomorphism. Since $\mathcal Z$ was arbitrary this is the required universal homeomorphism property. Together with steps 1 and 5 it gives all three equivalences and all three base-change assertions, separately.

source.place: Tag 0DTQ, injectivity, openness and surjectivity; omitted field-point details supplied
